method: reports/implement-v050/capture_structure.py over the 16 private sanitized Chase captures (gitignored fixtures-private). Output is numbered files, folder index, element counts, radio counts and distinct-value group counts only; no text, attribute values, file names or URLs.
owner_direction: 2026-11-20: the owner stated the existing personal, business, Benefits and card-selector captures are sufficient; no further live capture session was run.

findings.account_selector: Overview page has one mds-select: 4 options in the linked sign-in, 2 in the personal-only sign-in.
findings.card_selector: Benefits page card selector is native radio inputs in exactly one fieldset: 3 radios linked, 2 personal-only, exactly one checked, all radios unnamed (no name attribute), zero card-number-shaped ids.
findings.benefits_structure: Benefits captures have 6-8 section elements, 29-55 li rows and 3 mds-commerce-tile; detailed cards add 11-31 h3 headings; one card per sign-in shows one mds-progress-bar (tracker).
findings.loaded_state: Zero aria-busy elements in all 16 captures (captured in a completed state).
findings.offers_structure: Offers pages are structurally separate (navigation bar, no card-selector radios); owned by v0.6.

feasibility_estimate.basis: Measured Amex reads under the same WebView and 120000 ms budget (docs/archives/v0/v0.3/development/v0.3.0-last-phase-evidence.md): 4 cards, 12-13 pages, 71609-82789 ms, i.e. 5.5-6.9 s per page.
feasibility_estimate.chase_navigation: 1 Benefits page load plus 1 in-page selector switch per card (captures 3 and 12).
feasibility_estimate.conservative_rule: Count each selector switch as 2 page loads at 6.9 s.
feasibility_estimate.supported_scale_single_read: about 8 cards per read (1 + 2n page-equivalents <= 120000 ms at 6.9 s)
feasibility_estimate.live_confirmation: Phase 3 and the Definition of Done require three complete live reads within 120000 ms; a read that does not finish keeps existing data and reports partial coverage.

probe_finding: The unrun traversal probe (chase-traversal-timing-review-20261120.json) locks on a shared radio name; these captures show the card radios are unnamed, so it would have refused. Production selection must lock on the single selector fieldset instead.
